title: Chapter V · The office of contemplation

blocks.s: 6. With these and similar burning words the soul kindles its desire; so it shows its affection. With these incantations it calls the Bridegroom. And the Lord, whose eyes are upon the just and whose ears are open not only to their prayers (Psalm 33:16), does not wait for their prayers to end until they have finished speaking, but breaking into the middle of the prayer's course he hastens in, and runs quickly to meet the longing soul, drenched in the dew of heavenly sweetness, anointed with the best ointments: he restores the weary soul, feeds the hungry one, fattens the dry one; he makes it forget earthly things, wonderfully strengthening it by the memory of himself, giving it life, inebriating it, and making it sober again. And as in certain carnal offices the soul is so overcome by carnal desire that it loses all use of reason and the man becomes, as it were, wholly carnal, so rightly in this heavenly contemplation the movements of the flesh are so consumed and swallowed up by the soul that in nothing does the flesh contradict the spirit, and the man becomes, as it were, wholly spiritual.
